@austinrmiller, I fixed the issue description.

@tbosch Correct me if I am wrong, but if the original expression is static - `{'a': 'b'}` the workaround will have a slight difference that it will recreate the object at each change detection pass.

> [someProp]="{'a': x}"

also creates a new object  at each change detection pass (if I understood your question correctly)

With `{'a': x}` in the template I see `pureProxy1` being used in the aot generated code - https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/c33fda260726f5c050a75fc01fbd7a74800f8e37/modules/%40angular/core/src/linker/view_utils.ts#L183

Thus the object is recreated only when `x` changes (further optimization can keep the object around too). With the workaround it is recreated on each check, considered changed and repopulated in the DOM.

issue.title: Build with Closure compiler
issue.body:
This issue is here to track all the necessary changes in this library to make it work with the closure compiler with the least pain possible. 

My current understanding is that require changes, so far, boil down to "stringifying" property access in some objects.

body:
Any updates on this? Because of this issue all properties passed to ngTemlateOtletContext are not available when you try to access them in ng-template. The only workaround is to create context in component class (with normal, not quote syntax, because in compiled code in ng-template context properties are accessed with dot syntax) and pass this context to ngTemplateOutlet. But this is rarely used and passing variables in template more common:

```<ng-container *ngTemplateOutlet="someTemplate; context: { ...template variables here }"></ng-container>```

This bug seems to be even worse:

1. for actions, we seem to always strip quotes: We are just creating an `o.literalMap` which defaults to using no quotes for property names (see [here](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/packages/compiler/src/compiler_util/expression_converter.ts#L40))
2. for property bindings, we generate calls to `pureObjectDef`, which takes an array of property names (see [here](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/packages/core/src/view/pure_expression.ts#L21)). As we captured the property names during compilation, they won't get renamed.

Idea for the solution in `pureObjectDef`: Change it to receive an object literal, where we only use the keys. This way, closure compiler can also minify the property names. We already do this in other places in the view engine too...
